transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jin (Redwood SE), Lena (Novaforge VP Eng), Rahul (ML Infra), Sofia (Security), Tom (Product)

Summary: intake/discovery call for dedicated GPU capacity. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, heavy emphasis on tenant isolation, burst events (coordinated campaigns), predictable cost, and KMS / auditability for regulated PII workflows. They asked for a perf test and SOC2 docs.

Topics covered: current infra & constraints, expected steady-state QPS and surge patterns, isolation & tenancy models, encryption/KMS and audit logs, fallback strategies and model variants, timeline and success criteria

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena: Hi, Lena here. VP of Eng at Novaforge.
[00:07] Rahul: Rahul, ML infra.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia, security.
[00:11] Tom: Tom, product.
[00:13] Carlos: Carlos from Redwood, SE.
[00:15] Jin: Jin, solutions.
[00:17] Maya: Great. I'll kick off with context. We understand you're evaluating options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and a private deployment backed by your VPC. The goal today is to understand traffic profiles, isolation needs, and what a burst strategy looks like for you — is that about right, Lena?
[00:30] Lena: Yep. We run inference for a mix of chat assistants and batch reranking. Steady-state is moderate, but we have these marketing drops — like product launches — where traffic spikes by 6-8x for short windows. We're worried about noisy neighbor effects and also cost blowouts.
[00:48] Rahul: To add, the 99th percentile latency target is 350 ms for chat. We could relax to 500 ms for batch, but we need consistency. We tried an internal autoscaler but warmup time for the KV cache kills us.
[01:05] Carlos: Right, caching and KV are big. For Dedicated we can pre-warm KV and reserve capacity, minimizing that cold-start tail. There is also our adaptive prewarm logic — hmm, Red Wood Dedicate — sorry, Redwood Dedicated, that supports a warm pool.
[01:22] Rahul: (laughs) The transcript's already messing with your product name :)
[01:25] Maya: No worries. On isolation: can you tell us whether teams need single-tenant GPU nodes or if tenant fencing via containers/weights is sufficient?
[01:33] Lena: Ideally single-tenant for high-value customers. We have three tiers: internal, enterprise, and free-tier; enterprise workloads must be logically isolated and auditable. For cost reasons, free-tier can be multiplexed.
[01:45] Sofia: And from security, we need per-tenant audit logs, encryption with our KMS, and the ability to rotate keys without downtime. Also SSO/SAML for RBAC into the console.
[01:58] Jin: We support KMS integrations and per-tenant key policies, though the private path offers more direct KMS binding inside the VPC. For Hosted/Dedicated we do customer-managed keys via our KMS proxy — it's, um, that is documented — I'll send the note.
[02:14] Tom: If we go Dedicated, do we still get the same API surface as Hosted? We don't want divergent behavior.
[02:20] Carlos: Yes, same API. The runtime layer is consistent. The main differences are the tenancy and how capacity is provisioned. Dedicated is a reserved pool assigned to your org and supports pre-warmed nodes and guaranteed throughput.
[02:34] Maya: Let's surface the burst shapes. Rahul, can you walk us through a typical spike?
[02:38] Rahul: Sure. Normal QPS is ~120 rps for chat, peaks up to 900 rps during campaigns for about 20-40 minutes. Requests are short — median 30 tokens, but some users hit long context windows. Also we have batch rerank jobs that run nightly — heavy token counts.
[02:55] Carlos: Ok, so mix of short low-latency chat and high-throughput batch. For burst handling we recommend two levers: capacity reservation for baseline plus a warm pool for pre-warmed GPUs that can be brought into the pool fast, and secondly routing to cheaper model variants when needed.
[03:12] Lena: Model variant fallback is interesting, but our product team has strict quality thresholds. We need a measurable SLA for degradations.
[03:20] Tom: Yes, lowering quality affects NPS, not ideal. Is there an automated canary or A/B we can use?
[03:25] Maya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies tied to latency SLOs. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and model variants with measured token-level quality regressions — we can link the evaluation report.
[03:40] Rahul: How fast can you scale from baseline to peak? We're concerned about KV cache wall.
[03:45] Carlos: For Dedicated with a warm pool, we've seen effective scale in under 90 seconds for adding nodes and under 5s for adding threads on already-warmed nodes. Cold starts that require KV population can take minutes per model on large sequences. That's why we suggest keeping at least one replica warmed for your main model.
[04:03] Sofia: On auditability, can logs be pushed to our SIEM directly? We need JSON structured logs with request IDs and per-token cost attribution.
[04:12] Jin: Yes, we can forward logs to your SIEM over a secure connector, or you can store logs in your S3 bucket if Private. We have token-level cost & latency hooks already in the Console.
[04:25] Lena: What about burst billing? Do we pay pro rata for warmed GPUs in the warm pool even if not serving? We need predictable monthly costs for finance.
[04:34] Maya: There are two models: reserved capacity monthly commit which covers baseline and warm pool reservation charges, and a separate on-demand burst rate for short spikes beyond reserved capacity. We can model expected monthly cost given your traces — Carlos will generate a spreadsheet with assumptions.
[04:48] Rahul: For regulatory reasons, some datasets can't leave our VPC. How different is Private deployment from Dedicated?
[04:55] Carlos: Private is the private control plane and dedicated runtime in your VPC or on-prem. It gives you full data plane ownership. Dedicated (hosted) still routes inference through Redwood-managed runtime but with tenant isolation and encryption. If data residency is a hard requirement, Private is the path.
[05:12] Sofia: If we move to Private, does Redwood still manage upgrades and patching? We need patch windows and an on-call SLA.
[05:18] Jin: For Private we offer an ops-managed option where Redwood coordinates upgrades with your team; otherwise you self-manage. We can provide an upgrade cadence and outage windows in the contract.
[05:29] Maya: Let's talk SLA. What are must-haves?
[05:33] Lena: 99.9% availability for inference, and latency SLOs at 95/99 tailored by model. Also contractual data deletion and audit support.
[05:44] Maya: 99.9% aligns with our Dedicated enterprise tier. We can add contractual audit support and data retention controls.
[05:50] Tom: One other thing — tenant isolation against noisy neighbors. Is there a guarantee on maximum shared topology density?
[05:57] Carlos: Yes. For single-tenant nodes you get exclusive GPU. For multiplexed tenancy we have CPU/GPU quotas and eviction policies. We can also do GPU-level tenant fencing via MPS or the runtime's isolation shim. There are tradeoffs with cost.
[06:12] Rahul: Can you explain warm pool pre-warm heuristics? We have bursts that happen rarely but when they do we need performance.
[06:18] Carlos: Warm pool pre-warm can be static or dynamic. Static: you reserve N pre-warmed replicas. Dynamic: our autoscaler predicts bursts using historical traffic and can pre-start nodes based on schedule or anomaly signals. Dynamic is cheaper but the prediction accuracy matters.
[06:33] Lena: Prediction requires us to share historic traces, right?
[06:35] Maya: Yes, and that's why we'll ask you to upload traces. The more accurate the history, the better the warm pool plan.
[06:41] Sofia: For key management — we need to ensure plaintext never hits Redwood's control plane. How does key wrapping work?
[06:48] Jin: For Hosted we use envelope encryption with a customer-managed KMS key where you control master key in your cloud provider and we never store plaintext. For Private, keys live entirely in your environment. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[07:01] Carlos: Quick note on perf tests: we can run a 24-hour soak on Dedicated, with a synthetic burst window to measure tail latencies and warmup behavior. That requires sample model artifacts and tokenization parity.
[07:13] Rahul: We can provide model artifacts for a perf run? Some are third-party licensed — can we use a subset or a proxy workload?
[07:20] Jin: Yes, you can provide a synthetic workload that mimics your distribution. We can also run a baseline using a similar open model to surface latency shapes.
[07:29] Tom: About SLA credits and failover — if Dedicated in a region is exhausted, do you have automatic fallback to hosted model variants in another region?
[07:37] Maya: We offer smart routing policies. You can set fallback order: same model in another region, a compatible quantized variant, or queued requests. We also support token-level cost windows to prioritize critical traffic.
[07:51] Lena: How do you guarantee data residency if fallback routes to another region? We can't have EU customer data leave EU.
[07:58] Carlos: Fallback respects placement rules. If you set region constraints, we won't route outside those boundaries. Cross-region fallback is opt-in for customers who can tolerate that.
[08:09] Rahul: What's the procurement timeline? We're hoping to decide this quarter.
[08:13] Maya: Typical procurement for Dedicated is 4-8 weeks once we have capacity sizing and contract terms. Private deployments can take longer, 8-12 weeks depending on network and compliance reviews.
[08:24] Tom: Pricing ballpark?
[08:25] Maya: I'll share tiered pricing. Roughly it's committed monthly reservation based on GPU type + usage overage rates. We'll model with your traces.
[08:34] Lena: Ok. A couple of clarifying Qs: 1) Can we pin model versions and force rollback? 2) Is there a way to audit inference model provenance?
[08:42] Carlos: Yes on version pinning and rollback — rollouts are controlled via the Console with canary percentages. For provenance, we keep signed model manifests and checksum metadata and can surface it in audit logs.
[08:55] Sofia: We want to ensure SSO integration with SCIM provisioning.
[08:58] Jin: Supported. We'll share SSO/SCIM guides.
[09:03] Maya: Any blockers that would make you choose Private immediately?
[09:07] Lena: If legal says PII can't leave our network, that pushes to Private. Otherwise Dedicated looks attractive because ops overhead is lower.
[09:16] Rahul: Also cost — Private can be more expensive ops-wise.
[09:19] Maya: Understood. Let's capture next steps: Carlos will produce the burst-sizing spreadsheet, Jin will send KMS/SSO docs and a VPC sketch, and Maya will send pricing + SLA templates and SOC2 artifacts. Novaforge will provide traces and a list of models to test.
[09:37] Tom: Sounds good. One more: will Dedicated support gpu-level isolation for enterprise customers on our account?
[09:42] Carlos: Yes, single-tenant GPU nodes are available in Dedicated reserved pools for enterprise add-on. We'll map that in the pricing.
[09:50] Lena: Ok let's schedule the architecture deep dive next week, after you review our traces.
[09:55] Maya: I'll send a calendar invite. Anything else?
[09:58] Sofia: If you can include a sample audit log format in the SOC2 packet that'd be helpful.
[10:03] Jin: Will do.
[10:05] Maya: Great. Thanks all. Meeting end.

--- End of transcript ---

Notes: minor transcription artifacts present (Red Wood vs Redwood). References shared: pricing deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/dedicated-pricing), SOC2 kit (internal link), sample S3 upload link for traces (shared during call).

Recap (as sent in follow-up):
- Redwood to model cost using provided traces and deliver a detailed reserved vs burst pricing sheet (Carlos).
- Redwood to provide SOC2, KMS integration doc, and SSO/SCIM guides (Jin/Maya).
- Novaforge to upload traffic traces and list of models for perf test (Lena/Rahul).
- Schedule: architecture deep dive w/ private deployment specialist next week (Carlos).

End.
